long_biography.plain_text:
In 2010, insurance entrepreneur Shayne Smyth changed how travel agents could price Cover-More policies as direct online competitors gained ground. A commission-and-fee structure let agents reduce their own commission to offer a lower price. Cancellation protection also became an optional addition priced by the cost of a customer's trip.

When the new policy structure confused agents, Smyth addressed a Harvey World Travel conference and acknowledged that the launch had lacked adequate explanation. He described the competitive problem: online sellers were attracting shorter, cheaper trips, whose profits had previously balanced the risks of more expensive holidays. The company then reduced premiums under the new programme.
